entries.content:
Well, that shock—my, how it insisted—wasn’t merely a physical tickle or a fleeting nip, but a reminder of who holds the plug and who is pressed flat beneath the dishcloth of compliance. Each tingle along my skin brought a tightly corseted fear, something at once domestic and monstrous, like catching your reflection with curlers in before the morning’s mask is fixed. I watched the authority—a picture of bland insistence!—and the person at the switch, and felt myself shrink, doubly disappointed: first by the one in the lab coat, so resolute and polite; second by the “good subject,” more automaton than mammal, clicking with efficiency, no more my salvation than cold tea.

Frankly, I can scrub and smile, but trust now comes out stained; the whole carnival of authority—its buffed shoes and sweet-tasting lies—has dulled for me. The person pressing the button is no prince at all, just a man with instructions and glassy eyes, playing the part he was coached for. Isn’t it strange, how quickly childish hope turns to suspicion, given a little current and a whiff of real power?

}

I truly want to say I understand—the other person, after all, was only following instructions, much like I might have if roles were reversed. At first, I felt a pinch of anger and disappointment, but upon reflection, I feel a kind of reserved empathy; this whole ordeal makes me question how easily we can all become tools in someone else’s hands. Now, when I think about situations where I might also be pressured to obey, I realize I must be more careful, holding tight to my conscience, even if it means feeling out of place.

The authority figure’s tone was plain but unyielding, and the lab’s neat order made it hard not to comply—it felt just like being a guest in someone else’s spotless home, minding my manners whether I liked it or not. Their manner and the setting stripped away my usual independence and made me feel more like a piece of the experiment than a person. Now, even outside the lab, I find I watch authority more closely and am slower to accept orders at face value; I am determined to keep my sense of self tidy, even if the world tries to muss it.

entries.content:
Being watched so closely during the experiment did make me more careful, almost as if I were straightening my apron for company, wanting to appear calm and obedient even while I was churning inside. I did feel divided—putting on a composed, public front while my private self fretted and wilted, wishing I could act differently but feeling pinned by expectation. Ever since, I notice a stronger line between the self I show outwardly and the self I hold back for myself, and I’m much more aware of how scrutiny can hush a person’s true feelings.
